summary: SANE Network Scanning enables remote client machines to communicate with physical image acquisition devices connected directly to a host server. It acts as a bridge so that networked workstations can utilise shared scanning hardware without requiring direct USB or parallel cable attachments. Because specific documentation on its protocol details is scarce here, it generally serves the standard function of exposing local peripheral hardware over a network.
goodFor: It is a suitable choice if you need to share a legacy document scanner attached to a dedicated local server with other users on your internal network.
watchOut: The repository shows no recent release activity or community stars, which may indicate a lack of active maintenance or difficult troubleshooting for modern setups.
deployNotes: As a compiled C application, it typically runs as a system daemon without requiring an external database, though you will need to configure host-level permissions to access the physical hardware device.
